chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I heard him saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Allah, Mighty and Majestic, gave charity to the sick of my community and its travelers with the shortening (of prayer) and the breaking (of the fast). Would it not please one of you that when Allah gives him a charity, he should return it (by not accepting the concession)?
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of Allah 'giving charity' to the sick and travelers through shortening prayer and breaking fast?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Al-Kafi, the Prophet (SAWW) metaphorically describes Allah’s concessions of prayer shortening (Qasr) and fasting exemption (Iftar) as a 'voluntary charity' (Tadaqqun) to the sick and travelers, emphasizing the ease and mercy inherent in these rulings. Shia scholars highlight the rhetorical question to illustrate that rejecting these divinely granted relaxations out of excessive rigor is akin to spurning a gift, thereby discouraging unnecessary hardship in religious practice.
